lesson_title: Why Your Car Is Not Alive
hook_text: A car eats fuel, breathes oxygen, poops out gas and moves. So why isn't it alive?
clip_script: A car takes in petrol. It burns it with oxygen to release energy. It pushes out waste gas. It moves. Sounds alive. But scientists have a checklist of seven. Nutrition, getting food. Respiration, releasing energy in cells. Excretion, removing waste your body made. Growth. Reproduction. Sensitivity, noticing changes. Movement. A goat does all seven by itself. A mealie plant does too: it makes food from sunlight, grows taller than you in a few months, makes seeds, bends towards light and turns its leaves. A car? It never grows. It never has baby cars. It only reacts when someone drives it. And it has no cells. Fire fails too: no cells, no growth of its own kind. And one trap: respiration is not breathing. It is energy released inside every cell, even in plants, day and night.
visual_style: A whiteboard car and a goat side by side with a seven-row checklist; ticks fill the goat column, the car column gets crosses at growth, reproduction and cells.
mood: Playful challenge with a satisfying answer.
pacing: Quick tease, rapid seven-item checklist, side-by-side verdict.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and test anything around you against the seven.
